title: Add support for gzip-compressed output in mergecap and editcap
description:
Wireshark supports compressing the output file to a gzip archive
via wtap API. For mergecap and editcap, if the output filename
has the extension .gz, then the gzip compression would be used
to store the output.

Fixes #12385

You should reuse this option name and make the support generic for all tools.

I checked the commit you mentioned https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/commit/c14ea41233fa92a1cb97ef29d1f9ded6587e45a5

I think in this commit, the changes have effect only for the dumpcap, not for other tools (such as tshark).

Dumpcap also seems to use `ringbuf` API, whereas the application in this MR does use the `wtap` API. (and don't use ringbuf at all). Furthermore, for options where you have to choose for more than 2 options, this is not done with `capture_add_options` (for example - `wtap_name_to_file_type_subtype` / `merge_string_to_idb_merge_mode`.

If we go this way, where should I place the function that returns all the possible output format? I think I will need to keep the added fields to the `compression_types` structure in `wiretap/file_wrappers.c` (because I need to be able to convert the string to a enum compression type).

> If we go this way, where should I place the function that returns all the possible output format?

wiretap/file_wrappers.c.

Please note that "can I write a file compressed with this compression type?" and "can I write a file of this type as a compressed file?" are different questions - some file formats, such as Microsoft's Network Monitor format, cannot be written as compressed files because, when writing them, the code to write the file has to go back and rewrite earlier pars of the file.  Compression only works when the file is written 100% sequentially. `wtap_dump_can_compress()` takes a file type/subtype value as an argument and returns `true` if it can be compressed when writing and `false` if not.

Sure, I did the changes you suggested, @guyharris @stigbjorlykke 

Can you have another pass, please?

It's unclear if `LONGOPT_COMPRESS_TYPE` is `--compress` or `--compress-type`, and here it looks like the old use is removed in favour of the new. This does not work because it removes existing functionality.

Because we already have this option I think we should use `--compress-type` for all tools. For `tshark` we need to understand the difference between the existing option (feeding to dumpcap) and the new option (compress using wiretap).

I applied your change regarding `--compress-type` for `tshark` / `editcap` / `mergecap` `text2pcap` to keep consistency across all tools.  

I checked the documentation for the `dumpcamp` (https://www.wireshark.org/docs/man-pages/dumpcap.html) and there is no mention about the `compress-type`.

In the current option, if we use feeding to dumpcap (generated from tshark), we would store one more additional file. By using the current MR, the file would be directly written as wanted format.

> I checked the documentation for the `dumpcamp` (https://www.wireshark.org/docs/man-pages/dumpcap.html) and there is no mention about the `compress-type`.

That's probably because `--compress-type` is, in dumpcap, a greasy hack.  It silently does *no* compression if you're capturing without a ring buffer, and, at least from a quick look at the code, compresses a ring-buffer file, *after* it's been completely written, in a separate thread.

I'm not sure the rationale for this, but we should, at minimum, support compression regardless of whether we're using a ring buffer or not ("we can multithread it if we're doing a ring buffer but we can't do that if we're only writing to one file" is not much of an excuse).

> In the current option, if we use feeding to dumpcap (generated from tshark), we would store one more additional file. By using the current MR, the file would be directly written as wanted format.

I'm not sure what you're saying here.

dumpcap does not use libwireshark (and never will - a goal of dumpcap is to have as little code as necessary, as it may have to run with elevated privileges); it has a smaller library that reads only pcap and pcapng (when capturing from a pipe) and writes only pcap and pcapng.

> It's unclear if `LONGOPT_COMPRESS_TYPE` is `--compress` or `--compress-type`

It's currently `--compress-type` in all programs that support it, meaning "dumpcap and tshark", but I think it's only passed on to dumpcap in tshark.

I might vote for just `--compress`, with a compression-type argument, with `--compress-type` supported for backwards compatibility, because `--compress-type` sounds like "we always compress; this option specifies a compression type other than the default", while `--compress` sounds like "this option enables compression".

> I'm not sure the rationale for this, but we should, at minimum, support compression regardless of whether we're using a ring buffer or not ("we can multithread it if we're doing a ring buffer but we can't do that if we're only writing to one file" is not much of an excuse).

Do you think it may be a good idea to focus on solving the compression for the tools using `wtap` in this MR? I can open an issue for checking the dumpcap.

> I'm not sure what you're saying here.

I wanted to express that if we use the combination of tshark and dumpcap for generating a compressed archive, it would store one additional file, if this is even possible. 

> I might vote for just `--compress`, with a compression-type argument, with `--compress-type` supported for backwards compatibility, because `--compress-type` sounds like "we always compress; this option specifies a compression type other than the default", while `--compress` sounds like "this option enables compression".

For this, I saw for an option, it would work with any prefix that does not match anything else. For example, 

`./run/tshark -r ~/cap1.pcapng --print-timers` would produce the same output as 

`./run/tshark -r ~/cap1.pcapng --print-timer`. 

But 

`./run/tshark -r ~/cap1.pcapng --print` would produce a different output, since it matches another option.

So, backwards-compatibility would be ensured by design. Should I go and change the option name from `--compress-type` to `--compress?`

> I wanted to express that if we use the combination of tshark and dumpcap for generating a compressed archive

If you're generating a compressed file as the output from a live capture, all that needs to be done is to fix dumpcap so that it does compression if you're *not* using a ring buffer.  TShark would be involved only as a front-end to dumpcap; it would just pass the "write a compressed file" option to dumpcap.

If you're not talking about a live capture, I don't see why dumpcap would be involved at all.
Keeping both options for backward compatibility is probably best. Then you need to add and use `LONGOPT_COMPRESS`, and not touch `LONGOPT_COMPRESS_TYPE` in this MR.

> If you're not talking about a live capture, I don't see why dumpcap would be involved at all

Yes, I was refering to a live capture. 

In the meantime, I tried running dumpcap with the `--compress-type` option and it doesn't have the expected behaviour (at least in this command)

```
dumpcap -a duration:3 -w /tmp/output.gz --compress-type gzip

file /tmp/output.gz
/tmp/output.gz: pcapng capture file - version 1.0
```

> Keeping both options for backward compatibility is probably best. Then you need to add and use `LONGOPT_COMPRESS`, and not touch `LONGOPT_COMPRESS_TYPE` in this MR.

For me, this seems to be a bit confusing to have the both options, especially with a very  simillar name. So, in `tshark` the only difference when using this option is that I open the save file with other compression format, the rest should be the same. This is why I think backwards compatibilty is already there.

Do you know a way to test if everything is still good for the `dumpcap`, as the `--compress-type` is not mentioned in the documentation?

> In the meantime, I tried running dumpcap with the `--compress-type` option and it doesn't have the expected behaviour (at least in this command)

Yes - as I mentioned in an earlier comment, it only works if you're doing a capture with ring-buffer options.

Ok, so if running with `ring-buffer` option, it works as you described:

```
./run/tshark --ring-buffer duration:10 -w /tmp/random --compress-type gzip && sudo file /tmp/random*.gz
```

So, to make a summary for the tshark, my changes would allow the following:

```
sudo ./run/tshark -r ~/test.pcapng.gz -w /tmp/test_file.gz --compress-type gzip && sudo file /tmp/test_file.gz 

/tmp/test_file.gz: gzip compressed data, from Unix, original size modulo 2^32 79224
```
To sum up, do you think we still should have different options `LONGOPT_COMPRESS` and `LONGOPT_COMPRESS_TYPE` ?

> So, to make a summary for the tshark, my changes would allow the following:
> 
> ```
> sudo ./run/tshark -r ~/test.pcapng.gz -w /tmp/test_file.gz --compress-type gzip && sudo file /tmp/test_file.gz 
> 
> /tmp/test_file.gz: gzip compressed data, from Unix, original size modulo 2
> ```

That doesn't involve dumpcap, just tshark.
yes, I agree on this. I was just confirming it works.

> all that needs to be done is to fix dumpcap so that it does compression if you're _not_ using a ring buffer

I checked on this and it doesn't seem a very easy change. If I go for this, should be in a different MR @guyharris?

> If I go for this, should be in a different MR @guyharris?

Yes.
Ok, so after this MR gets approved and merged, I will open an issue and check how easy is for tshark to be able to compress without the `--ring-buffer` option.

There's an issue that discusses how compression with a ring buffer works (i.e., at the end via a separate mechanism) - #19159.

> I'm not sure the rationale for this,

My guess is that it was easier for whoever implemented it to compress it at the end, even though it seems less than ideal.
What would be the next steps for me in order for this MR to gets merged?

Get the pipelines to work :-)

https://gitlab.com/radunichita99/wireshark/-/pipelines/1403723531

For gzip output in dumpcap, see #9311, which asks for that, and 
!422, which is where the current implementation was added.  As noted in [this comment for !422](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/422#note_438092836), "the new option is valid only [if] ringbuffer is used".  No rationale is given for doing compression after a file is written, rather than compressing as the file is being written.
In this MR I would like to use `LONGOPT_COMPRESS` for `--compress` and `LONGOPT_COMPRESS_TYPE` for `--compress-type` to clearly show the difference, and to not touch the existing option.

Hey @stigbjorlykke,

I did a rebase today to fit the changes in the main branch, could you have another pass please?

I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong, but it doesn't look like the output files are compressed.
```
% ./run/tshark --compress gzip -c42 -w ~/output.pcap
% file ~/output.pcap
/Users/stig/output.pcap: pcapng capture file - version 1.0

% ./run/tshark -c42 -w ~/output.pcap.gz
% file ~/output.pcap.gz
/Users/stig/output.pcap.gz: pcapng capture file - version 1.0
```

So, for this MR, for t-shark the `--compress` option works only when using an input file specified with `-r` option, not from live captures. It was a discussion in this thread between me and @guyharris .

After this MR would get merged, I will open an issue and check how difficult it would be to do the gzip compression for live captures as well (without the `--ring-buffer` option).
If `-r` is required for `--compress` I think it should fail with an explatation that `--compress` requires `-r` and does not work for live capture.

@radunichita99 One issue to note is that `tshark -r input.pcap -w output.pcap` will write in `pcap` format and `tshark -r input.pcap -w output.pcap.gz` will write in compressed `pcapng` format. Probably not as expected when using the filename magic.

My testing shows that both of those write to `pcapng` format, with the latter compressed. Though I agree that it's probably not expected that filename extension magic works for the compression type but not the file type.

Minor points:

It's possible to compile without support for compressing to gzip. Should the documentation and help messages reflect that, either with some sort of boilerplate ("if supported") or with an appropriate `#ifdef`?

I added support for writing to `lz4` while this MR was being worked, so it should hopefully be trivial to enable that. (Most of the change is probably additional documentation).
I added a default value for the variable in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/16863/diffs
Should this be backported to the 4.4 branch?

On the one hand, it's a very nice feature.

OTOH, I think it's confusing as is where live captures can't be compressed; I know @radunichita99 plans to work on that, but if backported that would probably need more documentation.
!16886 is a backport of this and related fixes. I believe it's acceptable for 4.4 now if you agree.

Surely someone is going to want to write compressed output to the standard out for further piping. Is there any reason why it shouldn't be allowed?
This should say "editcap"
If the user has asked for compression, why not write it to standard out?
Most everything in !16871 can apply to the other command line tools as well.

Editcap has some processing in order to write multiple files if there's a prefix, inserting a counter before the suffix. It probably doesn't work correctly with a two suffixes, the latter of which is compression - e.g., it will put the counter between "pcapng" and "gz" in `output.pcapng.gz`. That's largely a preexisting problem, except that we didn't support compressed output before so people probably didn't put two suffixes.

commits_data.title: Add support for gzip-compressed output in mergecap and editcap
commits_data.message:
Add support for gzip-compressed output in mergecap and editcap

Wireshark supports compressing the output file to a gzip archive
via wtap API. For mergecap and editcap, if the output filename
has the extension .gz, then the gzip compression would be used
to store the output.

Fixes #12385
